habitat: Pairs occur in lowland and montane forest and along adjacent forested streams, feeding mostly in the mid- and upper strata on mossy and lichen-covered branches.
summary: A common resident of forest. Newman calls it the only woodpecker in southern Africa with an unmarked olive-green mantle. The identification line gives a grey head, a red rump in both sexes, and a red cap in the male. The call is a shrill chee-wit, chee-wit, chee-wit, or weer-dit weer-dit weerditdit, depending on locality. Bill colour, eye, legs, wings and the underparts were not described. No sourced Kruger population figure was available, and that gap was left unchanged.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident of forest, and Avibase does not mark the Kruger occurrence rare or accidental, so status is resident and all twelve months are listed. The grey head, red rump and male red cap are Newman’s identification line. The description names the unmarked olive-green mantle and does not describe the underparts. The immature was not described. Bill colour, eye, legs and wings were not given. The only Kruger photograph found under an allowed licence is the male side at Ehlanzeni, partly behind a branch. The female side is from Addo and the male back is from uMgungundlovu. No front or flight photograph was found. The grade A call is from Wild Fig Farm. The catalogue row does not give a province. No sourced Kruger population figure was available, and that gap was left unchanged.
